evidence.note: 'Q3 on-time departures fell on the two routes diverted around the roadworks' states the thesis up front.
'On-time departures fell from 86% to 81% in Q3, and retiming the diverted routes is the Q4 test' summarises finding and action.

'The council's 90% target counts on-time departures only, so lost mileage can rise unseen' introduces a lost-mileage blind spot that no following title (s-4 to s-7) picks up; it does not connect to the diversion argument either side of it.
'12 Cross-town and 14 Cross-town fell 14 and 11 points while the network fell 5' evidences the s-1 claim.
'Away from the roadworks the other six routes held between 85% and 90% on time' follows s-4 as the control comparison.
'Mill Street closed in three phases from 7 July, and routes 12 and 14 ran the diversion without retiming' gives the cause.
'Planning and the depot disagree on why 12 Cross-town fell a further 4 points in October' extends into October and a dispute.
'Retiming 12 and 14 Cross-town for the diversion is the Q4 test, checked at the end of January' restates the s-2 title's second clause almost word for word.

rationale: The s-4 to s-7 titles build a clear chain (drop concentrated on diverted routes, others held, unretimed diversion as cause, October dispute) and the thesis appears at the start. But the s-3 title jumps to a lost-mileage blind spot that none of its neighbours connect to, and the s-8 title repeats the s-2 title's 'retiming is the Q4 test' rather than advancing from s-7. Under the binary descriptor, a title that does not connect to its neighbours and a repeated title each fail.
